records.d: Romans built with modular standardization: bricks, tiles, and concrete poured to standard forms across an empire. The building was systematized. The city was manufactured.
records.h: Standardized materials and concrete construction let Roman builders replicate structures empire-wide. The system was modular. The city was repeatable.
records.mj: Established - documented Roman modular construction; standardized building across empire.

records.d: The balloon-frame house of the 1830s industrialized homebuilding: standardized lumber and nails replacing timber framing. The house became a kit of parts. Construction accelerated.
records.h: Machine-cut studs and wire nails let small crews frame houses fast. The parts were standard. The home was prefabricated in spirit.
records.mj: Established - documented 1830s balloon framing; industrialized homebuilding.

records.d: Sears sold kit homes from 1908: entire houses shipped by rail, assembled by owners. The house arrived in boxes. The city was mail-order.
records.h: Pre-cut lumber and instructions let buyers build catalog homes. Thousands were erected. The home was a product.
records.mj: Established - documented Sears Modern Homes; kit houses 1908-1940.

records.d: Levittown rose in 1947: assembly-line suburbs, houses built in 26 steps. The suburb was manufactured. The city was a factory output.
records.h: Specialized crews repeated tasks across thousands of lots. The process was industrial. The suburb was mass-produced.
records.mj: Established - documented Levittown; mass-produced postwar suburbs.

records.d: Habitat 67 stacked prefabricated concrete modules into a housing complex in 1967: the modular city as architecture. The building was assembled. The module was the brick.
records.h: Factory-built concrete boxes were craned into place, forming varied apartments. The construction was modular. The architecture was systematic.
records.mj: Established - documented Habitat 67; modular concrete housing.

records.d: Manufactured housing in the 1970s put factory-built homes on the market at scale: the house as manufactured good. The city included factories' output. The home was mobile.
records.h: HUD-code factory homes shipped complete to sites. The quality was regulated. The market was affordable.
records.mj: Established - documented manufactured housing; factory-built homes at scale.

records.d: Japanese builders automated construction in the 1980s: Shimizu's SMART system built floors with robots. The site became a factory. The building rose automatically.
records.h: Automated systems assembled steel frames floor by floor. The construction was robotic. The site was vertical factory.
records.mj: Established - documented Japanese automated construction; robotic building systems.

records.d: Chuck Hull patented stereolithography in 1986: 3D printing was born. Objects would be printed, eventually buildings. The printer was invented.
records.h: UV lasers cured resin layer by layer. The process was additive. The future was layered.
records.mj: Established - documented 1986 patent; stereolithography invention.

records.d: Behrokh Khoshnevis published Contour Crafting in 2004: 3D printing entire buildings. The house would be printed. The concept was academic, then industrial.
records.h: The paper proposed gantry printers extruding concrete walls. The vision was whole structures. The research was foundational.
records.mj: Established - documented 2004 Contour Crafting; 3D-printed building concept.

records.d: Enrico Dini's D-Shape printed large stone-like structures by 2008: binder-jetting buildings. The printer made stone. The scale grew.
records.h: Powder-bed printing bound sand into structures. The material was stone-like. The scale was architectural.
records.mj: Established - documented D-Shape; large-scale binder-jet printing.

records.d: Winsun printed 10 houses in 24 hours in March 2014: the stunt that launched construction printing. The world noticed. The printer built a street.
records.h: A giant printer extruded concrete houses in a day. The speed was the story. The industry was born.
records.mj: Established - documented March 2014 Winsun demonstration; 10 printed houses.

records.d: Winsun printed a villa and a six-story building in 2015: printing went vertical. The printer built up. The scale was proven.
records.h: Multi-story printed structures demonstrated height. The engineering was real. The vertical was printed.
records.mj: Established - documented 2015 Winsun structures; multi-story 3D printing.

records.d: Dubai opened a 3D-printed office in May 2016: the first printed commercial building. The office was printed. The emirate bet on printing.
records.h: The 250-square-meter office was printed and assembled. The statement was governmental. The bet was strategic.
records.mj: Established - documented May 2016 opening; 3D-printed office.

records.d: Apis Cor printed a house in 24 hours in 2017 with a mobile robot: the printer drove to the site. The robot built the house. The machine was mobile.
records.h: A rotating robotic arm printed the house on-site. The mobility was the innovation. The site was the factory.
records.mj: Established - documented 2017 Apis Cor house; mobile construction robot.

records.d: ICON printed a permitted house in Austin in March 2018: the printed home went legal. The code approved. The house was real.
records.h: The Vulcan printer built a code-compliant home. The permit was the milestone. The home was legal.
records.mj: Established - documented March 2018 ICON house; permitted 3D-printed home.

records.d: ICON printed a neighborhood for the homeless in Tabasco in 2019: printing served the poor. The technology had a mission. The street was printed.
records.h: Multiple printed homes formed a community. The purpose was social. The mission was housing.
records.mj: Established - documented 2019 Tabasco project; 3D-printed community.

records.d: PERI printed a house in Germany in 2021 with the BOD2: European printing went residential. The continent printed homes. The code was German.
records.h: The gantry printer built a code-compliant German home. The standards were strict. The home passed.
records.mj: Established - documented 2021 PERI house; German 3D-printed home.

records.d: MX3D's 3D-printed steel bridge opened in Amsterdam in 2021: the printer built infrastructure. The bridge was printed. The city walked on it.
records.h: Robotic welding printed the steel bridge in place. The structure was load-bearing. The infrastructure was printed.
records.mj: Established - documented 2021 MX3D bridge; 3D-printed steel bridge.

records.d: ICON's Wolf Ranch broke ground in November 2022: 100 printed homes, the largest printed neighborhood. The subdivision was printed. The scale was residential.
records.h: The Vulcan system printed 100 homes in Texas. The project was commercial. The neighborhood was the product.
records.mj: Established - documented November 2022 Wolf Ranch; 100-home printed community.

records.d: By 2023, Dusty Robotics' layout robots were marking construction sites: robots drawing the blueprints full-scale. The plan became the floor. The layout was robotic.
records.h: Mobile robots printed layout lines from BIM models. The accuracy was millimeters. The rework fell.
records.mj: Emerging - real products; robotic construction layout.

records.d: FBR's Hadrian X bricklaying robot advanced in 2023: the robot that builds walls. The mason was mechanical. The wall rose automatically.
records.h: The truck-mounted robot laid blocks from 3D models. The speed was robotic. The wall was precise.
records.mj: Established - documented Hadrian X; robotic bricklaying system.

records.d: By 2024, multi-story 3D printing was advancing: printed apartment buildings rising. The printer went high-rise. The city printed up.
records.h: Larger gantries and new mixes enabled multi-story prints. The engineering was structural. The skyline was printable.
records.mj: Emerging - real projects; multi-story 3D-printed buildings.

records.d: By 2025, AI was planning construction: generative schedules, robotic coordination, digital twins of sites. The site had a brain. The city planned itself.
records.h: AI systems generated schedules and coordinated machines from BIM. The twin was live. The planning was algorithmic.
records.mj: Emerging - real products; AI construction planning and digital twins.
